report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of mutate.py: claims about mutation generation, filters, equivalence, coverage, and early-return docstring placement verified against code.
risks: covered_lines | medium | Coverage DB bit-order assumption may be wrong; docstring claims 'lines the test suite actually executes' but no spec for line_bits format in this chunk. | Inspect coverage.py schema and compare with sqlite3 output in test.

trivially_equivalent | low | Uses compile() on arbitrary source; docstring says safe because compile doesn't execute, but compile can raise other exceptions like MemoryError or RecursionError? In practice only SyntaxError/ValueError caught; other exceptions could propagate. | Review Python docs for compile() exceptions; consider catching Exception.
_fn_source | low | Returns empty string for lines; docstring says 'its lines' but it's always empty. | Check callers to see if second element is used.
covered_lines | low | If multiple .coverage files exist, only first is read; docstring doesn't specify precedence. | Check if multiple coverage files expected.

Mutant.find/replace | low | Properties return before/after; docstring claims field compatibility with Mutation but doesn't verify actual field names. | Cross-check with hand-written corpus Mutation class.

handoff.purpose: Defines mutation operator constants, no-go filters, coverage reader, Mutant dataclass, and mutation application helpers.

symbols.name: SKIP_PATH_PARTS
symbols.note: Tuple of path parts to skip.

symbols.name: SKIP_FUNCTIONS
symbols.note: Frozenset of function names to skip.

symbols.name: _is_display_constant
symbols.note: Walks AST to determine if constant is argument to display call.

symbols.name: _looks_like_a_guard
symbols.note: Checks if source contains any guard name substring.

symbols.name: covered_lines
symbols.note: Reads coverage sqlite DB from repo root and returns dict of covered lines per file.

symbols.name: Mutant
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with fields id, defect_class, file, function, line, before, after, operator; properties find and replace.

symbols.name: trivially_equivalent
symbols.note: Compiles two sources and compares structural fingerprints.

symbols.name: _code_fingerprint
symbols.note: Builds tuple fingerprint of code object excluding line tables and filenames.

symbols.name: _fn_source
symbols.note: Slices function source from text; returns (source, '') or None.

symbols.name: _mutate_tree
symbols.note: Applies one mutation operator to function source, returning unparsed source or None.

claims.text: Every mutant is checked to still PARSE. A mutant that breaks syntax is not a defect, it is a typo, and any tool would catch it
claims.why: _mutate_tree parses fn_src and returns None on SyntaxError; trivially_equivalent catches SyntaxError and ValueError from compile.

claims.text: the cheap way is to never generate the junk. Each rejection is COUNTED and named, so the filter can be audited instead of trusted.
claims.why: No counting mechanism is visible in this chunk; the comment is aspirational and the counting logic may be in generate() elsewhere.

claims.text: A mutant here can never be a product defect.
claims.why: The filtering logic that uses SKIP_PATH_PARTS is not in this chunk; cannot verify that all paths in the tuple are excluded.

claims.text: Cosmetic or self-describing methods: a changed repr is not a defect worth catching, and mutating one only teaches the detector to fire on noise.
claims.why: The usage of SKIP_FUNCTIONS is not in this chunk; cannot verify it is applied.

claims.text: Constants whose value is display text, not behaviour. Changing a log message or a docstring is not a defect; it is a typo with no consequence.
claims.why: The usage of _DISPLAY_CALLS is not in this chunk; _is_display_constant uses it but the filtering logic that skips such constants is not shown.

claims.text: Guard vocabulary. Real incidents in the hand-written corpus were all removals of exactly this kind of code, so a site matching it is worth far more than a random one. This is a PRIOR on where defects live, not a correctness claim.
claims.why: The usage of GUARD_NAMES is not in this chunk; cannot verify that sites matching guard names are prioritized.

claims.text: True if this constant is an argument to a printing/logging call.
claims.why: The function walks the AST and checks if any Call's function name (lowercased) is in _DISPLAY_CALLS, then checks if the node appears in arguments or keyword values.

claims.text: Lines the test suite actually executes, from an existing coverage file.
claims.why: The function reads a coverage database and returns lines based on line_bits, but without the coverage.py schema we cannot confirm the bit mapping is correct.

claims.text: A mutant on a line no test reaches is a GUARANTEED survivor: it cannot be caught by the gate, so measuring it only dilutes the score.
claims.why: The statement is logically plausible but depends on the gate's behavior, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: This reads a coverage database if one is present and returns {} if not — and the caller must treat {} as "unknown", never as "nothing is covered".
claims.why: The function returns {} when no .coverage file exists or on sqlite errors; it does not raise.

claims.text: One generated defect. Field-compatible with the hand-written corpus's Mutation where it matters (id, defect_class, file), so the same measurement code reads both.
claims.why: The Mutation class from the hand-written corpus is not in this chunk; cannot verify field compatibility.

claims.text: True if the two sources compile to IDENTICAL bytecode.
claims.why: The function compiles both sources and compares _code_fingerprint results.

claims.text: A mutant that compiles to the same code object cannot change behaviour, so it is undetectable by ANY method -- a perfect test suite, a perfect graph delta, a human.
claims.why: If bytecode is identical, behavior is identical; this is a logical truth.

claims.text: Bytecode identity catches only the trivial cases: a genuinely equivalent mutant with different bytecode still slips through, so this is a LOWER bound on equivalence and the residue stays unknown.
claims.why: The function only compares bytecode; it cannot detect non-trivial equivalence, so it is a lower bound.

claims.text: Compilation is not execution: compile() builds a code object and runs nothing, so this is safe on arbitrary repository source.
claims.why: compile() does not execute code; it only compiles to a code object.

claims.text: Structural fingerprint of a code object, recursing into nested ones.
claims.why: The function recurses into co_consts that have co_code and includes co_code, consts, co_names, co_varnames, co_argcount, co_kwonlyargcount, co_flags.

claims.text: Names and constants are included because a mutant that only changes a constant DOES change behaviour; what is excluded is line-number tables and filenames, which differ for reasons that are not the program.
claims.why: The fingerprint includes co_names and consts, and excludes co_filename, co_firstlineno, co_lnotab etc.

claims.text: (exact source of the function, its lines) or None if it cannot be sliced.
claims.why: The function returns (source, '') always; the second element is an empty string, not the lines. The docstring claims it returns lines but it returns an empty string.

claims.text: Apply one operator to one function's source, returning new source or None.
claims.why: The function returns ast.unparse(tree) or None in several paths.

claims.text: Uses ast.unparse on the whole function, which normalises formatting. That is FINE for this purpose and worth stating: the measurement compares the mutant against its own unparsed original, never against the raw file, so normalisation cannot masquerade as a change.
claims.why: The measurement code is not in this chunk; cannot verify that the original is also unparsed.

claims.text: AFTER the docstring, never before. Inserting ahead of it demotes the docstring from body[0] to an ordinary string expression, which makes a LITERAL appear out of nowhere -- an artefact of the generator that was measured suppressing detection of this operator from ~100% to 37%.
claims.why: The code removes the leading docstring expression if present, then inserts the return after the docstring, preserving the docstring as the first statement.

observations.what: _fn_source returns an empty string for the second element despite docstring saying 'its lines'.
covered_lines assumes line_bits bit order (byte_i*8+bit) without verifying against coverage.py schema.
trivially_equivalent only catches SyntaxError and ValueError from compile; other exceptions could propagate.
The module docstring claims 'mechanical' and 'unbounded' but the generation loop is not in this chunk.
